Welcome to Oakwood Primary School
Oakwood Primary school is a happy, lively school with strong links in the community.
The school has established partnerships with the University of Gloucestershire, Gloucestershire College and Cheltenham Ladies College, which provides our pupils with a wealth of opportunities to enhance their curriculum entitlement.
Oakwood also works closely with its partner school, Gardners Lane Primary School, under the leadership of Headteacher, Oliver Tuck.
We are proud to be part of the Gardners Lane and Oakwood Federation, working in close partnership with Gardners Lane Primary School to provide the very best opportunities, care and support for our children and families.
Under the acting co-headship of Mrs Hayet-Patino and Mr Jacks, Oakwood proudly maintains its own unique identity, values and strong sense of community, while benefiting from the shared expertise, resources and collaborative approach of our Federation.
Our close partnership enables both schools to share knowledge, experience and best practice, continually strengthening the quality of education and support we provide. We also benefit from shared services, including our dedicated pastoral team, Pupil Parent Support Worker, Attendance Officer and Site Manager, ensuring that our children, families and wider school communities are well supported.
At the heart of our Federation, Oakwood remains proudly Oakwood – a school with its own distinct character, values and identity, where our children, families and staff are at the centre of everything we do. Our partnership strengthens who we are, while allowing us to preserve and celebrate the unique community that makes Oakwood so special.
Together, we celebrate what makes each school special, while combining our strengths to create a caring, inclusive and ambitious Federation where every child has the opportunity to thrive.
Our aim is to work with you, as stake holders, to share your ambitions for your children and your knowledge of them. This will enable us to make sure that together we can celebrate their achievements.
Oakwood School is a non-denominational, Local Authority Primary school, educating children aged 4 to 11 years.
Please click here to view the school performance table.
Prospective parents are welcome to visit, if you would like to book a tour please contact the school office.
Mrs Hayet-Patino & Mr Jacks - Acting Headteachers

About Us
Our School Vision
Our school Aims and Values embodies our culture and ethos, where relationships are at the heart of every interaction. Supporting everyone in the whole school community.
Our priority under the leadership of the Acting Headteachers and Senior Leadership Team, is to ensure the safety of everyone and to promote and support emotional and physical wellbeing. It is the foundation upon which everything else depends enabling all to ASPIRE & ACHIEVE.
Our School Expectations
We are restorative in our approach, using a range of methods and strategies in order to maintain positive relationships amongst our school community. We aim to achieve this by following 3 core expectations: READY RESPECTFUL SAFE
These key words are used all around school to remind children of our behaviour expectations. Dojo points are rewarded to those children demonstrating these positive behaviours and work carried out in lessons to discuss and model what these key words mean in every day life.
Our School Values
Our school values are embedded in all that we do in school and are celebrated each week in our Celebration Assembly and through the award of Dojo points. Children are recognised for demonstrating these six values through their positive work attitudes and behaviours, communication and interactions with others and for going above and beyond.

MFL - French
At Oakwood, we aim to develop pupils’ curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world through the learning of French, in line with the Primary National Curriculum. We aim to equip pupils with a strong foundation in listening, speaking, reading and writing which will enable them to communicate effectively and prepare for future language learning. In lessons, we encourage pupils to demonstrate determination as they build linguistic knowledge, work collaboratively through teamwork, develop self-belief as confident communicators and show passion and respect for languages and other cultures. Our vision is for all pupils to leave primary school as motivated, resilient and culturally aware learners.

Smart Phone Free School
Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 & 3
The Federation of Gardners Lane & Oakwood Primary Schools is working in partnership with other local primary and secondary schools, as well as our parent communities, to encourage the delayed use of smartphones. We are committed to 'Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 and 3' to help us achieve our goal.
Why Smartphone Free?
A series of conversations with parents and professionals over the last few years have led us to this point. Collectively, our community has seen an increase in the number of concerning behaviour and safeguarding incidents related to primary age children passively using technology and having access to smart devices and social media apps. Parents tell us that they'd like to hold off giving their child a smartphone but, because everybody is doing it, it really is difficult to say no.
Simultaneously, we have seen a growing increase in local, national and international research around the dangers of children engaging with smartphones too young. Some of the statistics are, frankly, quite frightening. As well as this, we feel it is time to address some of the false-information leading to parents feeling a need to get their child a smartphone.
On the 23rd September 2025, Bournside School hosted an event for parents, carers and education professionals to hear from guest speakers from PAPAYA, Smartphone Free Childhood and the University of the West of England. The messages were powerful - check out the slides and read through the statistics here.
September 2025 - A United Response
At the beginning of the 2025-26 academic year, 15 local primary schools came together to share a united letter promoting a play-based childhood over a technology-based childhood.
Over the course of the next year our schools will be adapting policy and sharing regular messages that will help us move towards a smart-phone free culture.
Navigating the online world with young children throws up a whole host of new conversations and challenges for parents. Let us be your partners on this journey. This page is here to provide you with a range of different resources and signposts to help you in your own learning about keeping your child safe online and having a partner by your side when saying no to your child about their repeated request for technology. We have to make our decisions as parents on what our children need; not just what they want. Being able to explain 'why' makes those conversations just a little bit easier...
PAPAYA - Parents Against Phone Addiction in Young Adolescents
The team at PAPAYA strive to help families thrive in the digital age. Their aim is to help parents and young people make informed choices about smartphones, social media and screens. Check out their website here and also search for their associated Facebook page.
Smartphone Free Childhood
As parents, there can be an overwhelming pressure to get your child the next digital device, simply because your child tells you all of their friends have it. No parent wants to be the only one saying no. Learn more about the Smartphone Free Childhood pact via the link here. You might be surprised to already discover how many of your child's classmates are already committed to a play-based-technology-reduced childhood.
Their tagline is simple: 'because children deserve a safe digital world'. The wealth of resource on this website is simply fantastic. Start with a simple filter by age and then really dig in to find out different ways you should be supporting your child's age-relevant development in the world of technology.

The Role of the Governing Body
The Governing Body takes a strategic role in running of the two schools. This means the Governors work with the Headteachers and Senior Management Team of each school to decide what they want the schools to achieve and set the framework for getting there by:
The Governing Body acts as a 'critical friend' to the Headteachers and staff by providing advice and support. it does this by offering constructive advice, a sounding board for ideas, a second opinion on proposals and help when needed. Remote Learning
At Oakwood Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that every child can continue to access high-quality learning when remote education is required.
Our remote learning provision aims to be engaging, accessible and supportive, following our school curriculum wherever possible. Learning activities and resources are primarily shared through ClassDojo, with additional support and alternative arrangements available for families who may need them.
We recognise that every child's needs and family circumstances are different, and our staff are here to help ensure that learning at home remains a positive and meaningful experience.
Our Remote Education Provision document, available below, explains our approach, expectations and the support available to children and families.
Useful Learning Links
Oak National Academy – Free online lessons and resources covering a wide range of curriculum subjects.
BBC Bitesize – Engaging videos, quizzes and activities to support learning across the curriculum.
Times Tables Rock Stars – A fun and interactive way to develop multiplication and division skills.
If you require any additional support with remote learning, please contact your child's class teacher. We are always happy to help!

Maths
We want all pupils to achieve their best and have a passion for mathematics, they are supported to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, to reason and problem solving through a variety of routine and non-routine problems. We want Oakwood children to have self-belief with a ‘can do’ attitude, believing that all children can be successful mathematicians and develop a growth mindset. Pupils at Oakwood are encouraged to embrace mistakes as a learning opportunity, having determination and understanding that mistakes are good and they help to grow our brains! Oakwood children have the opportunity to experience Maths through formal lessons, practical experiences and hands-on learning, both individually and as part of a team.

Music
It is our aim to develop children’s musical competence and confidence, building on fundamental musical skills while inspiring all pupils to develop the foundations of a lifelong love of music. Through a carefully sequenced and engaging curriculum, pupils revisit and build upon key musical concepts in a range of contexts, allowing their understanding to deepen over time. Our varied musical experiences spark pupils’ passion, nurturing enjoyment and encouraging a lasting appreciation of music beyond the classroom. Through collaborative ensemble work, pupils develop teamwork, learning to listen carefully, keep in time and contribute to a shared musical outcome. We strive to nurture a creative and reflective mindset through regular opportunities to perform, compose and listen; these experiences also build self-belief and determination, enabling pupils to grow in confidence, persevere through challenge and recognise their own musical potential, so that they can participate confidently and achieve successful outcomes by the end of each key stage.

Mental Health & Wellbeing
Remember it is good to talk! Please don't ever hesitate to contact your child's class teacher if you need advice but in the meantime here are some materials you may find useful:
TIC+
TIC + Counselling Services In Gloucestershire is a free and confidential service for children aged 0-25 and parents living in Gloucestershire.
They have a parent support line and an online chat feature called 'TIC+ Chat'.
The different services all have different phone numbers and operating times so check the website for the service you want.
CAMHS
CAMHS (Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service) have put together a range of resources to support children and their families who may be struggling with anxiety during these difficult times. There is a specific section covering the impact of coronavirus, but also more generic links to books, apps and websites.
Facts 4 Life
Facts4Life is a new way of thinking about our health which challenges commonly held beliefs about illness and builds resilience.
Childline
Winston's Wish
Winston's WishWinston's Wish is the leading childhood bereavement charity in the UK, who offer support & guidance to bereaved children & their families.
Relaxation
Making time to relax your mind and body can really help your wellbeing. There are endless resources on the internet but here are a few you that you may find useful. Click the links to find out more:
The Mental Health Foundation
Wellbeing Packs

Attendance
What to do if my child is absent?
Please ensure that you contact the school office before 9:00am on the first day of absence.
Why is regular attendance so important?
Being in school every day that it is open, is important to your child’s achievement, wellbeing, and their wider development.
Here’s what the data shows:
There are only a small number of circumstances where missing a school day is permitted.
When can my child be absent from school?
When you register your child at school, you have a legal duty to ensure your child attends that school regularly.
This means that your child must attend every day that the school is open, unless:
These are the only circumstances where schools can permit your child to be absent.
Can I take my child on holiday during term time?
Parents should plan their holidays around school breaks and avoid requesting leaves of absence for holidays unless it is unavoidable.
As leave of absence is only granted in exceptional circumstances, it is unlikely that your child’s headteacher will agree a leave of absence for a family holiday.
If permission is refused and you keep your child off school on the days requested, you are likely to be committing an offence and be issued a fixed penalty notice or be prosecuted by your local authority.
Where can I get support to help my child attend school?
Children may struggle to attend school for a wide range of reasons.
Please make contact with school at the earliest opportunity so that we can support you to improve school attendance.

E-Safety
Parents and carers have information via the website about keeping children safe online with peers, the school, other education offers they may access and the wider internet community.
We have set out the school’s approach, including the sites children will be asked to access and set out who from the school (if anyone) their child is going to be interacting with online.
Parents have been offered the following links:
Information for Parents
Our letters are designed to raise awareness of current Internet Safety issues as well as providing advice and further information.
Please speak to a member of staff at school if you are worried about anything online.
TikTok - Guide for Parents
MOMO - Guide for ParentsFortnite - Guide for Parents
Advice for Parents and Children
Help your child stay safe on social networks
Parents E Safety Guide Book
We tell our children to share but online it's different.
In fact sometimes sharing online can be dangerous. That's why we're asking parents to be Share Aware and keep children safe online.
http://www.nspcc.org.uk/preventing-abuse/keeping-children-safe/share-aware/
The internet is a fantastic learning tool and now forms the basis of much of our working and social lives. It allows us to communicate freely and quickly with people all over the world.
Whilst it has many positive benefits, there are sadly instances in which it can place our children in danger. Part of our responsibility as a school is to protect our children whenever they are online – this is both in and out of school.
We have put together a Parents' E-Safety guide and leaflet which is shared with children as a part of the curriculum.
The “Thinkuknow” website is brought to you by the Child Exploitation and Online Protection (CEOP) centre.
Kidsmart gives you lots of advice on how to stay safe online.
CEOP (The Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre) delivers a multi-agency service dedicated to tackling the abuse and exploitation of children in the real and ‘e’ world. Often it is referred to as an online 999. By clicking on the button, young people and parents can get advice on a range of issues such as viruses, hacking and dealing with bullying online.

Friends of Oakwood (F.O.O.)
Friends of Oakwood (FOO)
We are a committee of staff and parents who plan, organise and run, fund raising events for the benefit of the children of Oakwood Primary School.
So far fundraising has helped fund trips to the pantomime, provide every child with a book at Christmas, buy equipment and costumes for school performances, provide team sports kits and every class is given a donation to keep the cost of school trips down. We also provide the prizes for the regular maths and reading competitions.
FOO Survey
We are reliant on the willingness of parents and staff to help make events a success. Help can come in many forms and if you feel you could help with any of the following please contact the office for one of our survey forms.

School Meals
Dinner menu
https://caterlinkltd.co.uk/school/gloucestershire-county-council/
Information
School dinners are priced at £2.95 per day, £14.75 per week
Please drop into the school office to arrange payment or to find out about paying for your child's school dinners online.
Our Catering Company
Caterlink are extremely proud to be providing meals to students within Gloucestershire County Council Schools. Caterlink are committed to giving pupils the opportunity to enjoy and benefit from a nutritious lunch. We pride ourselves in using fresh local produce, with all our food being cooked and prepared fresh on-site where possible. What's so special about Caterlink?
Great Food The food children eat in school is very important for their education. Not only does a well-balanced diet help with general health but establishing healthy eating habits at a young age can give them knowledge for the future. We understand the likes and dislikes of primary school children so we tailor our menus to encourage maximum uptake.
People are Key We invest heavily in our staff to ensure that you or your child receives the meal they deserve. We have a chef trainer and development team who are dedicated to supporting the kitchens
Free School Meals
Free School Meals can be a confusing topic so to clarify please find below:Universal free school meals (UIFSM) are available to all children in reception, year 1, and year 2, regardless of their family's income, while free school meals (FSM) are available to children whose families meet specific income or benefit criteria. You can apply for FSM as soon as your child start Reception.
If you think your child may be eligible for FSM, please apply here:
https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/schoolsnet/your-pupils/free-school-meals
